findings.reason: the section's whole claim to a working guard is that control, and as written it is vacuous for two of the three fixes the same paragraph authorises.
findings.text: the positive measure was widened to "the launch environment and prompt … carry the fix", matching a deliverable that offers three fixes (an MCP startup allowance, a faster server start, or a prompt-side route through a deferred-tool search), but the declared negative control still names only "with the startup allowance removed, the test of the launch environment must fail": if the node establishes that the server starts fast enough or that the harness defers the tools, no allowance is part of its fix and the removal changes nothing, so the control cannot fail — it measures a component the fix may not contain.

findings.reason: the probe must also record a deferred-tool listing (the run's one `ToolSearch` result carried `total_deferred_tools`), or the section's node-local measure cannot pass under the mechanism the section was just changed to admit.
findings.text: the fixed-arm acceptance is "the fixed one lists the anchored tools as offered or reachable" read from "its session-start `mcp_servers` status and tool list", but a session-start record binds only the tools present at init: under the deferral mechanism the plan now names as equally likely, a connected server's tools are absent from that list and surface only through a `ToolSearch` result, so the record the plan names cannot show "reachable" and the node can satisfy its own endpoint yet be unable to evidence it.

findings.reason: the sentence is offered as a hypothesis and the done-when requires the node to settle it by experiment, so the plan's endpoint is unaffected; only the strength of one evidential claim would change.
findings.text: the added sentence concludes that "the harness deferring MCP tools behind a search is as likely a mechanism as a slow connect" from the run's one `ToolSearch` having "reported 39 deferred tools", but that record carries `total_deferred_tools: 39` as a count with no membership, while the same run's init record lists 42 tools that exclude `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep` and `Agent` — so the 39 are at this evidence equally consistent with the harness's own unlisted tools as with MCP tools; the sentence is also imprecise about the statuses (the record shows `imas-dd` connected, `lucy2` needs-auth, `reckon` pending, `reckon-anchored-edit` pending, not "every server but one … pending").
